findings.summary: crates/athena-cli/tests/retry.rs is not among the reading's deliverables
findings.evidence: A change outside the listed deliverables widens the scope.

findings.summary: The permanent unit test slices the `## [Unreleased]` section of CHANGELOG.md, so it will fail once that entry moves under a version heading at the next release.
findings.evidence: Existing changelog tests in crates/athena-core/tests/refusal_corpus.rs:966-975 (and 1045, 1078, 2811, 2898, 2953) search the whole CHANGELOG with `include_str!("../../../CHANGELOG.md")` and never slice Unreleased. The plan's test asserts the ids and phrases inside the Unreleased slice only. Fix: Search the whole CHANGELOG.md, as the refusal_corpus tests do. The three job ids are not in the repository today (Grep found none), so a whole-file search still fails on the base code. Keep the Unreleased check for the verifier's one-time Grep, not for a test that stays in the codebase.

findings.summary: The plan says closing the remaining case needs a check that refuses work. That is not shown, and the request names information-giving as the preferred fix.
findings.evidence: The request says a refusal rule is allowed only when giving the stage the information cannot prevent the failure. Ids the reader writes into its reading could be resolved without refusing anything. For example, the recorded deliverables of every job id in the reading could be shown when the reading is presented for acceptance, or carried into the planner and critic briefs. Neither needs a refusal. Fix: In the CHANGELOG and doc comment, describe the follow-up as resolving job ids cited in the reading and showing their recorded shape before acceptance, an information fix. Do not say it needs a refusal check, and do not imply that a refused share would apply.
findings.location: Decision 8 and Risk 4 (limit: ids the reader introduces in its own reading)

findings.summary: The test should build its expected deliverable lines from each recorded deliverable's own action, not from a fixed `modify` prefix.
findings.evidence: `EarlierAttempt.reading_deliverables` is `action path` (reader.rs:54), and the fake reader can record `create` (fake.rs:294-298). The demonstration says it checks the quoted `modify {path}` line, while also saying the lines are read from Records. Fix: Format each expected line as `> {action} {path}` from `latest_reading().deliverables`, using the same formatting `carry()` uses.

summary: I read the code the plan names. The fix sits where the fault starts. `referenced_jobs` (topics.rs:533-560) reads only `followed_up_ids(request)` and `job_ids_in(request)`, and `read_once` (reading.rs:603-608) passes only the retried job's id, although `attempt.introspection` is already filled by `retry_cause` (retry.rs:80, 111-192). `referenced_jobs_section` (reader.rs:436-461) prints only each job's request and findings. Passing the attempt, resolving the introspection's ids through the existing `carry()`, and printing criteria and deliverables under "Referenced jobs" gives the reader the information it lacked and adds no refusal. The rule is unchanged because `refusing_check` reads `referenced` only through `continued_jobs` (checks.rs:522-534). Making `scoped_reading` `pub(super)` works for a test module inside `reading::topics`, and the `include_str!` paths resolve correctly. The real-path test in retry.rs compiles on the base code and fails there by assertion: the request `try again on {second}` names only the job being retried, so no "# Referenced jobs" section is printed. The Scenario reader records `modify README.md` (retry.rs:275), so the test's expected line exists. I checked the readers of the changed things: the only caller is reading.rs:603, plus the briefs.rs and lifecycle.rs heading assertions, the fake reader's `Job ` parsing (fake.rs:240-246), and the two `reading_source()` scanners. The dependents list covers all of them. Athena already raised that retry.rs is outside the deliverables, and the plan justifies it. My remaining findings are minor: a CHANGELOG test that will break at the next release, an overstated claim about the follow-up, and a small test-formatting detail.
